That’s for the people upstairs.”But Arsenal’s manager did confirm they are seeking reinforcements. “We are trying to improve the squad and until tomorrow night we are going to do that,” he said. “I have been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match, but I will get back on it now.”Barcelona have agreed an £8.6m deal to sign Jesus, who has entered the final year of his contract after falling down the pecking order behind Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres. The 29-year-old Brazilian was at Camp Nou to watch the 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday. The Barcelona manager, Hansi Flick, said: “He’s a top striker and of course for us very important, he can give us a lot of things and [I’m] very happy that he’s here.”However, the Spanish champions would like to sign another attacker after selling Ferran Torres to Paris Saint-Germain and are said to have not given up on Álvarez.Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Atlético have agreed a deal with Juventus for Jonathan David on an initial loan with an option to make the Canada forward’s move permanent next summer. But they are understood to be determined to keep Álvarez, who joined from City in 2024.Arsenal remain hopeful that the 26‑year‑old could change his mind but are believed to be monitoring several other attacking options. Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye was among the players on their shortlist but Manchester City are in advanced talks over a £65m deal for the Senegal forward. Arsenal missed out onMorgan Rogers to Chelseaand failed in an ambitious attempt to sign Vinícius Júnior, the Brazil forward signinga contract extensionat Real Madrid.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionArsenal have signedChristos Tzolisto replace Leandro Trossard on the left but Martinelli’s expected departure to Al-Hilal for a club‑record £56m sale would create a space in the squad, although Eberechi Eze is also capable of playing there.Martinelli, who scored six times in the Champions League last season but only once in the Premier League, was due to have his medical on Monday after being left out of Arsenal’s squad against Coventry on the opening weekend. His fee surpasses the £40m Liverpool paid Arsenal for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain in 2017.Vieira looks poised to join Hamburg, where he was on loan last season, for £8.6m.Explore more on these topicsArsenalAtlético MadridBarcelonaAl-HilalnewsShareReuse this content

title: Liverpool sign Barcola in £123m deal and expect Gakpo to stay after City offer £80m | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: Bradley Barcola is aiming to win the Premier League after completing his move to Liverpool from Paris Saint-Germain for an initial £106m
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: Bradley Barcola is aiming to win the Premier League after completing his move to Liverpool from Paris Saint-Germain for an initial £106m
Content: Bradley Barcola has signed a five-year contract at Liverpool.Photograph: Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenBradley Barcola has signed a five-year contract at Liverpool.Photograph: Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesLiverpoolLiverpool sign Barcola in £123m deal and expect Gakpo to stay after City offer £80mFrance international says title ‘one of my biggest dreams’Club rejected weekend Gakpo bid from Manchester CityWill UnwinMon 31 Aug 2026 12.38 EDTFirst published on Mon 31 Aug 2026 09.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBradley Barcola is aiming to win the Premier League after completing his move toLiverpoolfrom Paris Saint‑Germain for an initial £106m, which could rise to £123m. The France international has signed a five-year deal.Andoni Iraola has prioritised signing wingers this summer after replacing Arne Slot. Barcola follows the arrival of Victor Muñoz as the former Bournemouth head coach aims to rebuild the front line.“It took a long time but I’m really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play,” Barcola said. “I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League – it’s one of my biggest dreams in my life. It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term – that’s why I signed a long contract – and I hope I can do it.”Barcola, who will be 24 on Wednesday, was a long-term target for Liverpool, who have tracked his progress over a number of seasons. Completing the transfer has been delayed while PSG waited to make signings to compensate for the exit of the former Lyon player, who attracted interested from other clubs but was adamant that he was willing to join only Liverpool.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“When I knew about Liverpool’s interest in me, I didn’t ask questions and I knew it was a very big club for me,” Barcola said.The Frenchman will probably be Liverpool’s final incoming. The club are expecting Cody Gakpo to stay after rejecting an £80m offer from Manchester City for the Dutchman over the weekend. Liverpool would regard selling a first-team player at this stage as problematic because it would allow little time to source a replacement.Harvey Elliott is expected to join Valencia on loan for the season. The midfielder returned this summer from a similar spell at Aston Villa, where he failed to make an impression and although he was part of the pre-season plans, has failed to make the squad for the opening two Premier League fixtures.Liverpool have targeted younger players in this window, evidenced by the signings of Barcola, the 21‑year‑old Jérémy Jacquet and the 23‑year‑old Muñoz in the hope of building a squad for the long term.Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolParis Saint-GermainTransfer windownewsShareReuse this content

title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 11: Manchester City | Manchester City Women | The Guardian
description: Beth Mead and Niamh Charles are notable additions to the champions’ squad that looks just as strong as last season
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Beth Mead and Niamh Charles are notable additions to the champions’ squad that looks just as strong as last season
Content: Manchester City are jubilant after clinching the 2025-25 Women’s Super League crown with a 4-1 victory against West Ham Women in May. Photograph: Naomi Baker/WSL Football/GettyBeth Mead and Niamh Charles are notable additions to the champions’ squad that looks just as strong as last seasonByTom GarryMon 31 Aug 2026 19.01 EDTLast modified on Mon 31 Aug 2026 19.44 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGuardian writers’ predicted position:1st (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)Last season’s position:1stProspectsChampions again at last, after a 10-year wait, Manchester City now face an even tougher task: defending their title. They appear to have a good chance of succeeding, especially after keeping their star striker, Khadija “Bunny” Shaw. The WSL’s top scorer andbest player of 2025-26performed a dramatic U-turnby signing a new four-year contractin May rather than leaving on a free transfer, and that may prove crucial in continuing City’s positive momentum.Their squad looks to be of a similar strength to last season. The Brazil forward Kerolinleft for Barcelonabut Beth Mead arriving from Arsenal in essence replaces her. Similarly, the exit of left-back Leila Ouahabi will be compensated for by the acquisition of Niamh Charles from Chelsea. Perhaps the only minor question is whether there is sufficient depth to sustain a challenge in the Women’s Champions League as well as domestically, but the core of regulars looks as formidable as any club in Europe.The team scored plenty last term and had great success down the flanks, with the right-back Kerstin Casparij providing the joint-most assists in the division. Defensively they look solid. The most intriguing challenge could be psychological, as they switch from hunters to hunted, becoming the team that everybody wants to beat. They start at home to one of the promoted sides, Birmingham City, and first meet a fellow title hopeful – Arsenal – at the start of October, when they will aim to lay down a marker in the title race.Graphic showing how City finished in the past five seasonsOff-field pictureOwned by City Football Group and led off the pitch by the managing director, Charlotte O’Neill, and director of football, Therese Sjögren, City enter the season with anew women’s team buildingat the training centre. The £10m building offers everything from underwater treadmills to a barista-style coffee machine in the canteen, with every element tailored towards maximising performance for female athletes. Previously the women’s team sometimes had to share a gym with City’s boys’ academy.The managerAndrée Jeglertz’s first season could scarcely have gone better, as he oversaw a league and cup double. He arrived in Manchester after a relatively uninspiring spell in charge of Denmark women but his CV is full of extensive high-level experience, including a 2004 European title with the Swedish club Umeå. The 54-year-old is a calm presence on the touchline, unwavering in his belief that his team will “find a way to win”, and has avoided controversy in press conferences, which he handles assuredly.Star signingView image in fullscreenBeth Mead joins the champions from rivals Arsenal.Photograph: Kate Green/WSL/WSL Football/Getty ImagesMead was the headline signing on a free transfer after nine years at Arsenal. City are hoping that the England forward – the Golden Boot winner and player of the tournament at the 2022 European Championship – is not past her best, at 31, and can flourish across a three-year contract. She is the all-time leading assist provider in the WSL. Mead also has 81 caps and will want to be part of any Lionesses squad at next summer’s World Cup.Stat attackIf teams want to defend more effectively against the champions, they could start by focusing on free-kicks and corners. City scored at least twice as many set-piece goals as anyone else in 2025-26. As strong as they were elsewhere, this was their superpower.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionGraphic showing Manchester City led the Women’s Super League for set piece goalsSet for a breakthroughThe 18-year-old full-back Sacha Lewis signed her first professional contract with City in August, having been with the club since under-14 level. The younger sister of the club’s men’s first-team full-back Rico Lewis, she has been a regular for England Under-19s and has been named in the England Under-20 squad that will go to Poland for September’s Women’s Under-20 World Cup. She was the player of the season for Manchester City’s “Next Gen” team last term and, with City juggling European and domestic football, may get a chance in the first team.What they say“Our biggest challenge this year is to continue winning and, at the same, compete in other competitions and also want to win those. Winning in one year is one thing, but being able to win in the next year, that is even tougher. Of course we can do that [compete on multiple fronts] and we have good enough players to be able to play with one starting XI on Saturday and do a couple of changes on Wednesday and still win. That was our biggest challenge last year – we had too many good players that were not playing enough games, so this year we will have the possibility to explore the whole squad. Each player will be more important than they’ve ever been for the club” – Jeglertz speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live.Where are they playing their home games?The Joie Stadium is the women’s team’s usual home, across the road from the Etihad Stadium, where they will play two home league fixtures. Those will be against Arsenal on 4 October and against Manchester United on 14 February. The 7,000-capacity Joie Stadium, that hosted matches at Euro 2022, has been the women’s team’s home for more than a decade and they were unbeaten at home in the league last season. They haven’t lost a home WSL game at the Joie Stadiumsince a4-3 thriller against Arsenalin February 2025.On Friday 4 September at 1pm, Suzanne Wrack will be answering readers’ questions about the new WSL season for GuardianConversationsExplore more on these topicsWSL season previews 2026-27Manchester City WomenWomen's footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Fifa extends ban on man who secretly filmed female footballers in Austria | Women's football | The Guardian
description: Fifa has extended worldwide the ban on a former match official and SCR Altach employee found guilty of taking secret videos and photographs of members of the club’s women’s team
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Fifa has extended worldwide the ban on a former match official and SCR Altach employee found guilty of taking secret videos and photographs of members of the club’s women’s team
Content: The SCR Altach stadium, pictured in 2022.Photograph: Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe SCR Altach stadium, pictured in 2022.Photograph: Getty ImagesWomen's footballFifa extends ban on man who secretly filmed female footballers in AustriaFormer SCR Altach employee now banned worldwideMove follows pressure from players’ unionsSuzanne WrackMon 31 Aug 2026 12.06 EDTLast modified on Mon 31 Aug 2026 18.24 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFifa has extended worldwide the ban on a former match official and SCR Altach employee found guilty oftaking secret videos and photographsof members of the club’s women’s team.In February, a regional court in Feldkirch,Austria, handed the man a seven-month suspended prison sentence, a €1,200 (£1,046) fine and ordered him to pay the victims €625 (£545) each in compensation after he was found guilty of filming and taking photographs of players, including minors, in the changing room, gym and showers of Altach’s women’s team between 2018 and 2025.The sentence provoked outrage from former Altach players and more widely in Austria. After a request from the Austrian players’ union (VdF) and the global players’ union Fifpro, theFifadisciplinary committee extended on 4 August the man’s ban from football-related activities to a global one. A Fifa spokesperson said: “In line with article 70 of the Fifa disciplinary code, the Fifa disciplinary committee has extended the sanction imposed on an official by the Austrian FA to have worldwide effect.”Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.The man did not request a statement of the reasons for the decision within a prescribed timeframe, so the decision has become binding and final. Federations are able to ban individuals from football related activities only in their respective countries.Christos Papadimitriou, the women’s football coordinator at the VdF, said: “Anyone who secretly films players in the locker room crosses a clear line. The fact that the ban now applies worldwide sends an important signal: those who seriously violate players’ rights cannot escape the consequences by moving abroad.”The Czech players’ union, CAFH, hascalled for a lifetime banfrom all football-related activities for Petr Vlachovsky, the former coach of FC Slovacko, who was convicted of similar offences in addition to being in possession of child sexual abuse material. Vlachovsky was convicted in May 2025 and handed a suspended one-year prison sentence and five-year domestic coaching ban.In March Fifpro said: “Because the Czech criminal process and the Czech FA’s administrative proceedings are separate and can run in parallel, the union is challenging the FA to implement a lifetime football ban for Vlachovsky and all sexual offenders. Fifpro is exploring possible legal avenues on behalf of players to achieve a global ban.”Explore more on these topicsWomen's footballFifaAustrianewsShareReuse this content

title: Chelsea’s perfect yet unserious start to the Premier League season | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Xabi Alonso’s side have scored seven and conceded five in two wins so far, a product of the squad’s constant churn
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: Xabi Alonso’s side have scored seven and conceded five in two wins so far, a product of the squad’s constant churn
Content: Chelsea have won two games in chaotic fashion to start the new Premier League season.Composite: Guardian Design, Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenChelsea have won two games in chaotic fashion to start the new Premier League season.Composite: Guardian Design, Getty ImagesSoccer with Jonathan WilsonPremier LeagueChelsea’s perfect yet unserious start to the Premier League seasonXabi Alonso’s side have scored seven and conceded five in two wins so far, a product of the squad’s constant churnSign up for our free newsletter hereJonathan WilsonMon 31 Aug 2026 10.40 EDTLast modified on Mon 31 Aug 2026 11.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTwoPremier Leaguegames played for Chelsea under Xabi Alonso: two wins and seven goals scored. It’s the sort of start that would delight many new managers – only two other clubs can boast about a six-point start this Premier League season (albeit with Arsenal to play later on Monday). Points gained in this odd transitional phase, when almost nobody seems quite ready, could prove extremely valuable come the end of the season. And yet, for all the attacking potency, there must also be concerns about Chelsea’s openness and the five goals conceded.Context must also be considered, and it projects both ways. It’s early in the season. There has been, as ever, a lot of change at Chelsea. They will get better; they will achieve greater coherence. But equally there has to be a sense of realism about the nature of the teams they’ve played. Brighton may have thrashed a shambolic Aston Villa 4-0 last weekend, but they were missing seven frontline players at Stamford Bridge andstill put three past Chelseaon Sunday. And while Fulham looked very lively as Chelsea won 3-2 on the opening weekend, they couldn’t muster a shot on target against Sunderland on Sunday.Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s actionRead moreHow good are Brighton? Were Villa just terrible on that first weekend? Was it really just Granit Xhaka’s appeal for Sunderland to be themselves again that made a side that had lost at Ipswich capable of dominating Fulham through midfield? It’s very hard at this stage to trace any patterns, other than perhaps to say that Xhaka’s performance against Fulham showed whyChelseawanted to sign him in the summer.The systems are different, so the comparison perhaps isn’t entirely fair, but Xhaka, and his midfield partner Noah Sadiki, offered a level of control that Chelsea under Alonso have so far been entirely lacking – striking, given the degree of control Enzo Maresca insisted upon as manager last season. Both Chelsea games so far have felt almost like a pastiche of the modern Bundesliga: all high tempo and turnovers, chaotic and fun and slightly unserious.This is not how it’s meant to be. Alonso’s Bayer Leverkusen side, in which Xhaka was partnered in central midfield by one of Robert Andrich, Aleix García, or Exequiel Palacios, won the Bundesliga in 2024 conceding only 24 goals in 34 league games. They averaged 59.5% possession, whereas Chelsea so far this season have had just 32%. Perhaps when Moisés Caicedo returns to fitness – he managed 14 minutes from the bench on Sunday before being forced off again – his energy and mobility will bring an immediate improvement, but the way both Fulham and Brighton have at times sliced through Chelsea suggests there are structural issues.The usual criticism of the 3-4-2-1 formation used by Chelsea is that it is too blockish, that creativity comes almost entirely from the two inside-forwards, making the side playing it predictable if they dominate possession. Its usage, at least in the Premier League, tends to have been as a counterattacking system – this is how, for instance, Oliver Glasner deployed it at Crystal Palace over the last two seasons. Two holding players operating in front of a back three should provide the trapezoid shape that has become the default for sides hoping to guard against the counter. Yet with Roméo Lavia alongside either Reece James or Malo Gusto, that solidity has been lacking.Why, then, is Alonso’s system suffering the opposite problem? The issue really stems from a positive: Alonso’s 3-4-2-1 is not the blockish formation often seen. Rather it is a basis from which multiple variations stem. It has a variety that helps overcome a potential over-reliance on the two inside-forwards. That’s how, for instance, center back Maxence Lacroix ended up bursting through to set up a goal against Fulham. Breaking the lines and varying the pattern is part of the pattern.The defensive concerns predate Alonso. It’s been 18 games since Chelsea last kept a clean sheet, their longest run in the top flight since 1961. Whilethe signing of Emí Martínezshould give them a more assertive, less error-prone figure in goal than Robert Sánchez in goal, there will be issues, at least in the short term, in getting the balance right at full-back. Plus, defences are best when they are stable, when interactions become automatic; while Lacroix is the sort of central defender Chelsea have been short of and will almost certainly make them better in the long term, and while Josh Acheampong, who played well against Fulham and came off the bench against Brighton, looks a hugely promising presence (he started only eight league games last season); incorporating both of them while adapting to a new goalkeeper will take time. There is a cost to the constant churn at Chelsea.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionArsenal, next Sunday, will provide a far stiffer test. Chelsea’s front three of João Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer give them a puncher’s chance, but there is a chance Arsenal render them irrelevant by dominating the game through the midfield. They are two teams at very different stages of their development.This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US.Subscribe for free here.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueSoccer with Jonathan WilsonChelseaXabi AlonsonewslettersShareReuse this content

title: Elversberg and ‘miracle village’ prove that Bundesliga fairytales still exist | Bundesliga | The Guardian
description: German football has long insisted there is more to their elite league than a title race. Now they have a story that shows the world that surprise and wonder does indeed live here too
Author: Andy Brassell
Headline: German football has long insisted there is more to their elite league than a title race. Now they have a story that shows the world that surprise and wonder does indeed live here too
Content: David Mokwa of Elversberg celebrates scoring his team’s third goal in the 3-2 win over Bayer Leverkusen.Photograph: Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenDavid Mokwa of Elversberg celebrates scoring his team’s third goal in the 3-2 win over Bayer Leverkusen.Photograph: Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesBundesligaElversberg and ‘miracle village’ prove that Bundesliga fairytales still existGerman football has long insisted there is more to their elite league than a title race. Now they have a story that shows the world that surprise and wonder does live here tooAndy BrassellMon 31 Aug 2026 07.52 EDTLast modified on Mon 31 Aug 2026 11.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFriday night was no first day fun for VfB Stuttgart as they got first-hand proof of what the rest of theBundesligafeared: that Bayern Munich are perhaps mightier than ever. The curtain-raiser, though, didn’t actually set the tone for the the weekend. German football has long insisted there is more to their elite league than a title race, and now they have a story that shows the world that surprise and wonder does indeed live here too.Bayer Leverkusen arrived into their opening fixture of the campaign thinking their season might contain greater certainty than the last one, a more tranquil voyage after being blown off course by almost €300m of player sales and the ill-fated appointment of Erik ten Hag. Enter SVElversberg, Bundesliga first-timers and representatives of – a “miracle village” as Bild put it – Spiesen-Elversberg, a town with a population of just over 13,000, situated 15km north-east of Saarbrücken, 30 minutes’ drive from the French border.The miracle got big enough for all to see it on the Bundesliga’s inaugural Saturday afternoon. Seventy minutes into their top-flight debut and the locals gathered in the Ursapharm Arena – currently under a renovation programme to bring it up to a modest 15,000 capacity, with journalists covering the game from a temporary steel gantry on top of scaffolding and accordingly given a safety briefing beforehand – were pinching themselves. Vincent Wagner’s team led 3-0, courtesy of two goals in the space of 60 seconds in the opening 10 minutes, and then a third 25 seconds after half-time.View image in fullscreenElversberg players – and mascot – celebrate in front of their home fans after the 3-2 win against Leverkusen.Photograph: Thilo Schmülgen/ReutersNew Leverkusen coach Carles Martínez, who looked increasingly exasperated on the touchline as the game went on, threw a host of forwards on to salvage the game, and Patrick Schick and Christian Kofané both scored to reduce the arrears, but it wasn’t enough. A town with no train station and no town hall was now home to a team not only with a first-day Bundesliga win (and no team from Saarland had won a top-flight game since 1993 when FC Saarbrücken beat – you guessed it – Leverkusen), but a victory over the 2024 champions, no less. Even arriving in the same division was akin to a “moon landing”, Wagner had said before the game, continuing to say staying up would be their “mission to Mars”. August results may be notoriously fickle and this may seem like years ago by November, but the win was no fluke.And make no mistake, Leverkusen were shook from minute one. Elversberg pressed and rattled them, with the visitors’ new captain Edmund Tapsoba looking more the Bundesliga debutant, prone as Lukas Petkov opened the scoring and then turning over the ball almost from kick-off, as Cole Campbell swept into the area to bludgeon in a quickfire second.The Bulgarian midfielder Petkov had led from the front in the promotion campaign, scoring 13 and creating another six to pick up the slack after top scorer Younes Ebnoutalib left for Eintracht Frankfurt in the winter break. True to form, Petkov also created David Mokwa’s goal at the start of the second half, which turned out to be the difference with a delicious delivery from the right. Yet Campbell is really indicative of the step up. Bought from Borussia Dortmund for €6m in the summer, the 20-year-old from Houston has been rated for a while without truly making a dent in the top tier, either at BVB or on loan at Hoffenheim. He started here – as much of his team did – like a man on a mission, and having laid out a record fee, Elversberg need this to work too.View image in fullscreenElversberg fans celebrate during their team’s opening-day win.Photograph: Christian Kaspar-Bartke/Bundesliga/Getty ImagesThis spend needs to be put in perspective, of course. When Strasbourg full-back Guéla Doué (elder brother of Desiré) completes his move to the BayArena on Monday, it will be the fourth time this summer thatDie Werkselfhave spent in excess of €20m on a player. Leverkusen, and their coach, had no excuses. After an encouraging pre-season, they were beset by many of the old problems that undercut their Champions League hopes last season. Mark Flekken, their refreshingly blunt goalkeeper, could have been talking in March or May when he told the media: “I can’t even offer an explanation right now.”On the other side, it was all joy. Flekken’s opposite number Nicolas Kristof, whose brilliant save from Jonas Hofmann in stoppage time shut down Leverkusen’s last hope of taking something from the game, was one of two players in the lineup who has been at the club since they were in the regional fourth tier, winning promotion to the 3.Liga in 2022, at the end of his debut season at the club. It is already a fairytale. If they can build on their start as they build that main stand, it would be a story for the Bundesliga ages.Quick GuideBundesliga resultsShowBayern Munich 5-1 Stuttgart, Union Berlin 3-3 Eintracht, Leipzig 3-0 Mönchengladbach, Mainz 0-0 Paderborn, Elversberg 3-2 Leverkusen, Cologne 3-2 Hoffenheim, Dortmund 2-0 Hamburg, Freiburg 4-1 Werder Bremen, Augsburg 3-0 SchalkeWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Talking pointsBayern’sopening night brutalityhad been, as so often in the past, aided and abetted by their visitors Stuttgart, who tend to play in their normal front-foot style against the champions and are accordingly ripped to shreds even in games (like this one) in which they have good spells. Michael Olise was on the scoresheet but Harry Kane didn’t even need to score, while Ismaël Saibari offered enterprise and two assists from the bench. Vincent Kompany’s team are frightening.View image in fullscreenMichael Olise scores for Bayern Munich.Photograph: Angelika Warmuth/ReutersStill, Dortmund had taken hope from their second half in last week’s Super Cup and were very attractive in a one-sided first half against Hamburg, a departure from previous Niko Kovac teams. But although they cruised to a 2-0 win there was a huge blow, with new boy Giannis Konstantelias rupturing his ACL on his full debut, minutes after scoring the second. BVB now have to consider free agent replacements, with both Jadon Sancho and Reiss Nelson among the names circulating.Saïd El Mala, who nearly ended up at BVB, instead wore the FC Köln No 10 shirt for the first time and helped to inspire a comeback win against Hoffenheim, scoring a first equaliser before new signing Thijs Dallinga struck two memorable goals in a 3-2 victory.Elversberg’s aforementioned former star Ebnoutalib had an explosive start to the campaign, hitting a hat-trick at Union Berlin. It was an afternoon of vindication for the Moroccan striker, who scored on his Frankfurt debut against Dortmund in January and was then injured shortly after. “It’s good for my mind,” Ebnoutalib said after the game, even though an injury-time Tim Skarke equaliser snared Union a point after they had trailed 3-1 (and debutant Eintracht goalkeeper Noah Atubolu had needed to perform excellently to keep them at bay that long).Schalke’s return to the top flight started brightly at Augsburg, with Finn Dahmen keeping them at bay in the early stages before Michael Gregoritsch punctured his former club’s hopes with the opener, and it was virtually one-way traffic from there, ending with 10 men and a 3-0 loss. Still, they could be Werder Bremen, given a 4-1 Sunday kicking at Freiburg the day after their star man Jens Stage was confirmed as out injured until the new year.PosTeamPGDPts1Bayern Munich1432Freiburg1333Augsburg1334RB Leipzig1335Borussia Dortmund1236Cologne1137Elversberg1138Eintracht Frankfurt1019Union Berlin10110Mainz10111Paderborn10112Bayer Leverkusen1-1013Hoffenheim1-1014Hamburg1-2015Werder Bremen1-3016Borussia M'gladbach1-3017Schalke 041-3018Stuttgart1-40Explore more on these topicsBundesligaElversbergEuropean club footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Harry Edward, Britain’s first black Olympic medallist, inducted into England Athletics hall of fame | Athletics | The Guardian
description: Harry Edward, who won two bronze medals at the 1920 Olympics, will be honoured along with Mo Farah, Sonia Lannaman and Shirley Strong
Author: Neil Duncanson
Headline: Harry Edward, who won two bronze medals at the 1920 Olympics, will be honoured along with Mo Farah, Sonia Lannaman and Shirley Strong
Content: Harry Edward competes in the 1922 AAA Championships – he won the 100, 220 and 440yd titles within a single hour.Photograph: Courtesy of University of Westminster ArchiveView image in fullscreenHarry Edward competes in the 1922 AAA Championships – he won the 100, 220 and 440yd titles within a single hour.Photograph: Courtesy of University of Westminster ArchiveAthleticsHarry Edward, Britain’s first black Olympic medallist, inducted into England Athletics hall of fameEdward and Mo Farah among those to be inductedSonia Lannaman and Shirley Strong also honouredNeil DuncansonMon 31 Aug 2026 19.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBritain’s first black Olympic medal winner Harry Edward is to be inducted into the EnglandAthleticsHall of Fame. Edward will join the likes of Mo Farah, former sprinter Sonia Lannaman and medal-winning hurdler Shirley Strong, who will all be honoured at a ceremony in Birmingham in November. Edward’s citation includes the tribute: “A true citizen of the world and a pioneer of British sport, England Athletics is proud and humbled to induct Britain’s first black Olympic medallist into the Hall of Fame.”The remarkable story of Harry Edward: Britain’s first black OlympianRead moreEdward was until recent years a forgotten hero of the 1920s, a decade that saw him win two bronze edals, in the 100m and 200m, at the 1920 Antwerp Olympics. He was also three times the AAA 100yd and 220yd champion and won the 100, 220 and 440-yard AAA championships in 1922, inside a single hour. King George V came down from the stands to personally congratulate him.Soon afterwards he emigrated to the US and disappeared from view. When he died in 1973 not a single British newspaper published a line to mark his passing.Born and raised in Berlin, he was forging a promising career as a teenage sprinter when the first world war began. His father came from the British colony of Dominica, so Edward was arrested and interned. After the war he went to London, joined the Polytechnic Harriers and ran for Britain in the Olympics. Harold Abrahams, the British sprinter immortalised in Chariots of Fire, regarded him as one of the greatest sprinters he ever saw. He never beat him.After Edward emigrated in 1923, he devoted his life to fighting for civil rights and leading international programmes to help refugees and foster children. He had written an extraordinary autobiography, entitled When I Passed the Statue of Liberty I Became Black, but it failed to find a publisher. It sat unread in a box in a New Orleans archive, among his medals, photographs, scrapbooks and letters, until it was discovered and published in 2024 – making the William Hill Sports Book of the Year shortlist. Next year, English Heritage plan to erect a blue plaque on his old London home near Euston station.View image in fullscreenHarry Edward (right) crosses the finish line winning the 100 yards race at the 1920 AAA Championships at Stamford Bridge.Photograph: Topical Press Agency/Getty ImagesFarah, Britain’s most successful athlete of all time, is among this year’s other Hall of Fame inductees. Birmingham-born Lannaman was Britain’s premier sprinter of the 1970s and a favourite for medals at the Montreal Olympics in 1976 before injury scuppered her chances. She went on to win 100m gold at the 1978 Commonwealth Games and 4x100m relay bronze at the 1980 Olympics. Strong won silver in the 100m hurdles at the 1984 Olympics, having won Commonwealth gold in 1982.The three other three inductees are triple Paralympic gold medal winner Stephen Miller, who also co-founded the SMILE Through Sport organisation to encourage disabled people to participate in sport, the coach Mike Holmes, who guided Katarina Johnson-Thompson’s early career, and the photographer Mark Shearman, a fixture at major athletics events for more than six decades.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionTickets are availablefor the England Athletics Hall of Fame dinner and awards presentationat the Hilton Metropole Hotel, Birmingham, on Saturday 21 November. title: Transfer latest: Juventus in Woltemade loan talks, Everton agree £40m Balogun fee | Transfer window | The Guardian
description: Nick Woltemade is close to a loan move from Newcastle to Juventus, a year after arriving at Newcastle in a club-record £69m deal
Author: Louise Taylor
Headline: Nick Woltemade is close to a loan move from Newcastle to Juventus, a year after arriving at Newcastle in a club-record £69m deal
Content: Nick Woltemade has struggled to impose himself at Newcastle since joining from Stuttgart.Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Every Second Media/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenNick Woltemade has struggled to impose himself at Newcastle since joining from Stuttgart.Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Every Second Media/ShutterstockTransfer windowTransfer latest: Juventus in Woltemade loan talks, Everton agree £40m Balogun feeManchester City confirm Allan signing for initial £32.1mPalace sell Muñoz to Forest and poised to sign AhanorLouise Taylor,Will Unwin,Jacob Steinberg,Ben FisherandEd AaronsMon 31 Aug 2026 18.47 EDTFirst published on Mon 31 Aug 2026 05.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNick Woltemadeis close to a loan move from Newcastle toJuventus, a year after arriving at St James’ Park in a club-record £69m deal from Stuttgart. The gifted Germany forward has struggled to impose himself amid the high-intensity gameplans choreographed first by Eddie Howe and now Matthias Jaissle.Football transfer deadline day looms: latest news on Gakpo, Sarr and more – liveRead moreJuventus are one of a handful of clubs – Borussia Dortmund are among the others – to have inquired about Woltemade’s availability and Newcastle are in negotiations with the Turin club regarding a move involving a loan fee of about £5m.Any switch for the 24-year-old appears contingent on Matias Fernandez-Pardo completing a £51m move from Lille. The 21-year-old Belgium international was top of Jaissle’s wish list and is due in Newcastle for a medical. He can play across the front line, including as a No 10.Woltemade is unlikely to be the only player leaving before the deadline on Tuesday night. The winger Jacob Murphy is wanted by Nottingham Forest, Nick Pope – Jaissle’s third-choice goalkeeper – is looking for a new club and Besiktas retain an interest in Joe Willock.Pope, who started last season as Howe’s first choice and harboured then-realistic ambitions to be part of England’s World Cup squad, wants first-team football after falling behind the new signings Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen.Willock has impressed Jaissle and, despite offers from Istanbul, an exit that looked inevitable under Howe may be postponed.Everton have agreed a £40m fee with Monaco for the strikerFolarin Balogun. The USA international has attracted interest all summer after impressing at the World Cup, where he gained notoriety for having his red card punishment suspended after an intervention from Donald Trump.Although born in New York, Balogun was brought up in London and started his career at Arsenal. He made 10 senior Arsenal appearances , and had loans at Middlesbrough and Reims, before being sold in 2023 toMonaco, where he was the player of the year last season after scoring 13 goals in 30 Ligue 1 appearances.Balogun is regarded as a replacement forBeto, who has had a medical with Fiorentina after an offer of about £15m was accepted.The deal for Balogun limits the chances of Richarlison returning to Everton from Tottenham.View image in fullscreenFolarin Balogun (right) was in the World Cup spotlight after having his red card punishment suspended.Photograph: Jeff Chiu/APManchester City have confirmed the signing ofAllan Eliasfrom Palmeiras in a €37.5m (£32.1m) plus €2.5m deal. The 22-year-old wide forward made his debut for Palmeiras last year and has made 96 appearances for the club, scoring nine goals and making 12 assists.Allan is City’s third major acquisition of the window after Elliot Anderson, for £116m, and Ayyoub Bouaddi, for £85m. City are open to a loan for Jack Grealish, with Everton hopeful of taking the 30-year-old midfielder.“This is a surreal moment for me,” Allan said. “Manchester City, with everything they have won over the past 15 years, are one of the most attractive clubs in the world for players. To be able to sit here today and say I have joined them is the proudest moment of my life.”Crystal Palace are poised to sign the Atalanta defenderHonestAhanoron loan. The 18‑year‑old will join Chelsea on a permanent deal for £40m next summer but is due to gain experience of English football by spending this season at Palace.Palace have signed Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea so would not have been able to borrow Ahanor if he had completed his transfer to Stamford Bridge during this window.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionPalace have had a disappointing start, losing their first two games under Pierre Sage, and face an uncertain end to the window. Nottingham Forest have completed the £22m signing of the Colombia wing-backDaniel Muñozfrom Palace, reuniting him with Oliver Glasner, but have had a bid for Dean Henderson rejected.Palace are keen on the Eintracht Frankfurt midfielderHugo Larsson. The 22-year-old is a Sweden international.Liverpool are monitoring the Senegal winger Ismaïla Sarr but Palace are determined not to sell him or the midfielder Adam Wharton, who is of interest to Chelsea.Hull are interested in takingDário Essugoon loan from Chelsea. The midfielder joined from Sporting last summer but is not part of Xabi Alonso’s plans.Brighton are pushing to complete a deal for Millwall’sFemi Azeez. Millwall want £15m for the forward, who was in the 2025-26 Championship team of the season. Brighton are yet to meet the 25-year-old’s valuation but there is an expectation the deal will go through.Unai Emery said he expectsIbrahim MbayeandTaylor Harwood-Bellisto be Aston Villa’s final arrivals of the transfer window. Both attended Villa’s home defeat by Arsenal on Monday.Emery saidTammy Abrahamhas decided against a move to Ipswich and will stay at Villa to compete for his place. “Tammy Abraham’s decision is to stay here,” Emery said. “We opened the door for him but he’s decided to stay here with us. I am going to be very demanding with him to add his qualities with us.”Mbaye’s £47m move from Paris Saint-Germain and Harwood-Bellis’s £25m signing from Southampton are expected to be finalised on Tuesday.Explore more on these topicsTransfer windowNewcastle UnitedJuventusEvertonMonaconewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Pain-free’ Alcaraz brushes aside qualifier in US Open return after four months out | US Open Tennis 2026 | The Guardian
description: Carlos Alcaraz beat Roman Safiullin 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 in the first round of the US Open in his first match since April
Author: Tumaini Carayol
Headline: Carlos Alcaraz beat Roman Safiullin 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 in the first round of the US Open in his first match since April
Content: Spain's Carlos Alcaraz wore tape under a sleeve on his right arm to protect his wrist.Photograph: Kena Betancur/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSpain's Carlos Alcaraz wore tape under a sleeve on his right arm to protect his wrist.Photograph: Kena Betancur/AFP/Getty ImagesUS Open Tennis 2026‘Pain-free’ Alcaraz brushes aside qualifier in US Open return after four months outSpaniard beats Roman Safiullin 6-4, 6-4, 6-4Alcaraz has not played since April with wrist injuryTumaini Carayolat Flushing MeadowsMon 31 Aug 2026 18.35 EDTLast modified on Mon 31 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAsCarlos Alcarazedged closer to the conclusion of his first singles set in more than four and a half months, like so many times in his career instinct took over. Up 5-4, 30-15 in set one, Alcaraz swept forward to the net behind a precise wide serve and, when his opponent Roman Safiullin responded with a dipping backhand return directly to his feet, Alcaraz delicately pushed a half-volley over the net for a winner.It was a gorgeous shot, a perfect example of the creativity and feel trademarked by Alcaraz that has been missed throughout his extended injury layoff. That touch of genius was followed, predictably, by a wide smile, a quick hold and a comprehensive victory as the Spaniard returned to competition with a stellar 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 win against Safiullin.Aryna Sabalenka begins US Open title defence with victory against Camila OsorioRead moreWith Alcaraz marking his return to competition at a grand slam tournament with no warmup or match preparation, there was a lot of uncertainty about his level and how his wrist might react to ramping up so dramatically to the best-of-five-sets format. The enormous ball striking of Safiullin, meanwhile, also made this a particularly curious first-round match as it was tough to say how exactly Alcaraz’s wrist would hold up while absorbing such pace.All things considered, this was an incredibly positive start. From the beginning, Alcaraz shook off his own lingering doubts and lack of certainty about the wrist by eviscerating his own forehand, the best in the world, throughout the match. He struck it brilliantly from the outset, dominating from the baseline as he fired down 20 forehand winners to just nine forehand unforced errors. The few times he trailed in service games, he hit himself out of trouble.“It’s pain-free right now,” Alcaraz said of his wrist. “I felt great. I don’t know how it looked from outside but, from inside, my feeling was that I was hitting normal. I was playing pretty normal, playing my style, and the arm, the wrist, everything felt great. I’m going to still take care of it, obviously, these days and before the matches and everything, but I’m just really happy it’s pain-free finally.”The one curiosity, though, is Alcaraz’s serve. As was the case in the mixed doubles, where Serena Williams even served first in their second match, Alcaraz kept his speeds low, averaging just 113mph behind his first serve. Alcaraz has worn tape under an arm sleeve in all of his matches and practices, and it is logical that he should treat the wrist cautiously by not trying to serve as hard as possible so soon into his comeback. However, not being able to win many free points will have a bearing on how far he can go here.For now, Alcaraz has no choice but to take things day by day and see how things unfold with so much uncertainty ahead. On his first day back – as his parents, brothers, his team and even the rapper Travis Scott watched on from his box – things could have hardly gone any better. “It was a difficult day for me, to be honest, but at the same time, a really beautiful one,” Alcaraz said.“[I] started the day really nervous. Really, really nervous, thinking: ‘I’m going to make it, I’m going to compete again.’ I had more nerves than usual, but just happy, because for me, my goal here is to compete, to enjoy, and let’s see how my body’s going to react after the matches, after the competition again.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“I don’t know how far I’m going to go in the tournament. I didn’t know if I was going to lose this one, if I’m going to make the second round, final. I don’t know how far I’m going to go. But what I just really want to do is enjoy every time that I’m going to walk into the court feeling the energy from the people, feel the competition, walking up, I’m thinking, all right, it’s match day. That’s what I’m going to do this tournament.”Explore more on these topicsUS Open Tennis 2026Carlos AlcarazUS Open tennisTennisnewsShareReuse this content
